name: Lienzer Altstadt
kurzbeschreibung: The sun-drenched old town of Lienz enchants as the jewel of East Tyrol with southern charm, vibrant townhouses, Liebburg castle, and Dolomite views.
tags: Leinz (or 'Lienz' if referring to the city)
beschreibung:
Overview

The enchanting historic old town of Lienz—proud district capital and vibrant heart of East Tyrol—stretches across the confluence of the Isel and Drau rivers at an elevation of 673 meters. Blessed with over two thousand hours of sunshine each year, the town exudes a relaxed southern alpine atmosphere that earned it the moniker "Sun City" (Sonnenstadt). The pedestrianized central town square, lined with palm trees, brightly painted merchant facades, and welcoming pavement cafés against the dramatic limestone backdrop of the Lienz Dolomites, offers one of the most idyllic townscapes in the Austrian Alps. With its charming plazas, sunny promenades, and friendly shops, the old town forms the bustling focal point of the entire region.

Route & Requirements

Lienz boasts a storied heritage: nearby Roman Aguntum was already a flourishing regional hub in antiquity, and Lienz was granted town privileges in 1242 by the Counts of Gorizia (Görz). The focal point of the historic center is the lively Hauptplatz, dominated by the magnificent early 17th-century Liebburg castle whose twin onion-domed towers serve today as town hall. Historic stone fountains and intricately decorated facades bear witness to the enduring prosperity of this former trading center on the Drau. Strolling through the pedestrian lanes reveals gothic burgher residences with arched courtyards, specialty craft boutiques, and historic taverns. A scenic walk leads to the gothic parish church of St. Andrew, housing valuable winged altarpieces and ancestral tombs of the Gorizia counts. Perched above the town stands Bruck Castle, former residence of the counts, now housing a celebrated museum with works by Albin Egger-Lienz.

Visit & Arrival

The pedestrian precinct is open 24/7 year-round with free public access. Transit connections: frequent ÖBB trains arrive via Spittal an der Drau or through the Puster Valley to Lienz railway station, located only three minutes on foot from Hauptplatz. By car: via the Drautal road B100 from Carinthia, Felbertauern road B108 from Salzburg/North Tyrol, or B100 from South Tyrol; underground parking is available at Hauptplatz and Dolomitenhalle.

Tips

The entire town center is paved with flat cobblestones and fully barrier-free. Do not miss the colorful Lienz farmers' market held on Saturdays, where local producers showcase Schlipfkrapfen ravioli and artisanal Pregler schnapps. Relax beneath palms at an outdoor café on Hauptplatz while admiring jagged Dolomite peaks. Sample fresh river trout from the Isel Valley in a traditional inn and savor an authentic espresso.
